title: SLO dependency weave and staff mapping proposal
content:
Purpose:
This is a working proposal for weaving service-level objectives (SLOs) into the engineering and ops staffing plan across platform and feature teams. The idea: treat SLO adoption as both a dependency graph and a staffing runway — map owners, signals, and handoff nodes so rollouts don’t create coverage gaps during launch windows.

Quick summary (tl;dr):
- Define a Dependency Weave: a compact mapping of service-to-service SLO impact (who affects who) with primary+secondary owners.
- Create a Staff Mesh: identify 30/60/90 staffing touchpoints (feature team lead, platform steward, SRE responder, product PM).
- Run a 6-week cross-functional sprint to validate alerts, dashboards, and escalation flows for three pilot services (model-serving, routing, KV-cache).
- Acceptance = automated alert-to-runbook handoff for >90% of high-severity signals and a staffed on-call matrix during canary phases.

Context / motivation:
We keep seeing launch friction where model-serving changes increase downstream latency and nobody quickly knows the chain of impact. Existing SLO docs are siloed: product teams define SLOs, SREs own dashboards, platform teams own capacity. The weave aligns responsibilities explicitly, reduces finger-pointing, and makes oncall staffing predictable during rollouts.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- SLO dependency analysis approach (how to trace impact)
- Staff mapping template (roles, escalation lines, on-call coverage for rollouts)
- 6-week pilot plan with milestones and deliverables
- Minimum telemetry, dashboards, and runbook acceptance criteria
- Known risks and mitigation checklist

Out of scope: long-term SLO governance (>12 months), billing-level quota policies, legal/compliance reviews (separate cadence).

Stakeholders (recommended):
- Platform Engineering: staffing coordinator and deployment policy owner (Aisha / Miguel)
- Serving Runtime team: model-serving SLO authors (lead: Claire)
- Site Reliability: escalation lead + runbook curators (Omar)
- Product (Hosted API): rollout PM and customer-impact contact (Janelle)
- Observability: metrics ingestion and dashboard templates (TBD)
- Solutions Eng / Support: customer comms and remediation play (rotating)

Terms and roles (short):
- Primary owner: team responsible for fixing root cause for a violated SLO
- Secondary owner: team accountable for mitigation and customer comms until primary resolves
- Steward: platform-level person who coordinates cross-team fixes and triage
- On-call responder: the individual who must act on alerts in the first 15 minutes of an incident

The Dependency Weave (method):
1) Inventory SLOs: pull existing SLOs for the three pilot domains (model-serving, routing, KV-cache). Catalog signal names, thresholds, and current owners.
2) Trace impact edges: for each SLO, map upstream services it depends on (e.g., model-serving latency -> GPU scheduler queue length, KV-cache miss rate -> embedding fetch latency).
3) Annotate edges with impact type: latency / error / saturation / capacity.
4) Produce a minimal graph with 2-hop dependencies and attach primary/secondary owners to each node.

Deliverable: a compact CSV + one-page dependency map for each pilot service (concrete output: dependency-weave-pilot-YYYYMM.csv).

Staff Mesh (template):
Columns for template: service, primary owner (name), primary team, secondary owner (name), secondary team, steward, oncall responder roster (30/60/90 day), escalation contact, SLA response time (T1/T2/T3).
Example row (draft):
- service: model-serving
- primary owner: Claire Nguyen (serving-runtime)
- secondary owner: Omar Siddiqui (SRE)
- steward: Miguel Hernandez (platform)
- oncall responder roster: week 1-2 Claire team (canary), week 3-6 SRE paired with Claire, week 7+ handback to feature oncall

6-week pilot plan (high level):
Week 0 (prep): dependency inventory, align owners, create dashboards
Week 1-2 (hardening): establish baselines, add synthetic tests and alert thresholds
Week 3 (canary): enable canary traffic and monitor error/latency SLOs, runbook dry-run
Week 4 (escalation drills): trigger simulated degradation (load test/TTL bump) and execute notify-oncall flow
Week 5 (rollback/runbook validation): validate automations — alert -> incident ticket -> owner assignment -> remediation checklist
Week 6 (retro + decision): decide go/no-go for broader rollout; capture lessons and update weave

Milestones and owners: (short list)
- M1: Inventory complete and weave diagram created (owner: Platform) — due +10 days
- M2: Dashboards and alerts live for pilot signals (owner: Observability) — due +17 days
- M3: Canary traffic enabled with staffed oncall (owner: Product + SRE) — due +24 days
- M4: Escalation drill completed and runbook updated (owner: SRE) — due +32 days
- M5: Decision and roll-forward plan (owner: Platform + Product) — due +42 days

Minimum telemetry & runbook acceptance criteria:
- Telemetry: request latency histogram (p50/p90/p99), error rate, queue depth, CPU/GPU utilization, cache hit ratio, key business metric (e.g., tokens/sec served).
- Alerting: alerts must include service owner, suggested next step, runbook link, and knock-on downstream notifications when appropriate.
- Runbook: runbook must list initial triage steps (0-15m), mitigation steps (15-60m), known rollback conditions, and postmortem owner.
- Automation: at least 1 alert -> Slack bridge -> PagerDuty escalation path wired for the on-call roster.

Staffing / capacity notes (estimates):
- Pilot week oncall coverage estimated at 1.5 FTEs (shared across teams) for the canary week.
- Platform steward time: 0.2 FTE for 6 weeks (or equivalent 8-12 hours/week) to coordinate meetings, produce artifacts.
- Observability lead: 0.3 FTE to create dashboards and alerts.
- SRE escalation lead: 0.5 FTE during drill week.
Assumptions: teams can spare these allocations; temporary rotation prioritization will be honored.

Communications and rituals (recommended lightweight cadence):
- Weekly 30m sync: platform steward + primary owners + SRE + product PM
- Twice-weekly pulse during canary: 15m (quick readouts on SLOs)
- Daily incident window during drill week if any alert fires
- Shared Slack channel with pinned artifacts (runbook links, dashboards, escalation matrix)

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: missing ownership for a 2-hop dependency (who owns the cache layer). Mitigation: require explicit owner for every node in the weave before canary.
- Risk: alert fatigue / noisy thresholds causing false positives. Mitigation: use synthetic traffic baselines and mute non-actionable signals for the pilot.
- Risk: staffing conflicts (vacation, support). Mitigation: identify backup responders and pre-authorize swaps.

Decision points (what needs executive signoff):
- Go/no-go to require SRE-backed oncall for any public-facing canary (recommended): signoff by Head of SRE + Head of Product.
- Permanent ownership changes (if weave shows recurring primary fails): exec signoff and org-level reassign.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- TODO: confirm Observability owner and ETA for dashboards (Miguel to ping).
- TODO: produce CSV schema for weave (fields + sample row).
- Q: Should we include cost signal (GPU queue cost) as SLO input? Pros/cons — include in pilot?
- Q: How to coordinate with Dedicated/Private customers where contract SLAs differ? (Janelle to coordinate with CS)

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Align owners for three pilots (Aisha to confirm by 2026-09-18)
- Schedule kickoff + 30m inventory session (calendar invite: "weave kickoff")
- Draft CSV template and initial dependency export from our metrics catalog

Meeting notes (from 2026-09-10 pre-sync):
- Claire: willing to own primary for model-serving pilot but needs 2 backfills for canary week
- Omar: SRE can provide escalation responder but only if dashboards are complete 72h before canary
- Product: Janelle wants customer-impact play added to runbooks
- Action: Platform to build dependency map and publish Slack channel by 09/17

Appendix (artifacts to add to this doc):
- proposed CSV schema (to paste)
- example runbook template (to paste)
- minimal dashboard wireframe (screenshot link once available)

Notes on tone: keep this doc lightweight and practical. The goal is to make it easy for teams to say "yes" to the pilot by reducing unknowns and explicit staffing asks.

If you want to iterate: add your comments inline (use Slack thread or edit the doc). I'm going to push a short PR to the ops-scripts repo that adds a starter Prometheus query set for pilot signals (https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/56).

-- Aisha
